page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-32 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance offering 32 dedicated vCPUs on an arm64 architecture alongside 256 GB of system memory. Designed with a memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8 GB per core, this configuration prioritizes workloads that demand significant memory capacity relative to compute resources, operating without simultaneous multithreading overhead or x86-specific instruction sets.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, leaving disk persistence to attached cloud block storage volumes. Network connectivity provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring deliberate network design or additional routing resources for public ingress and egress. The absence of local scratch disks also requires applications to rely on remote storage architectures for stateful workloads.

Cost efficiency is influenced primarily by the density of the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio on an Arm-based execution platform. Arm architecture generally delivers favorable energy efficiency and lower resource allocation costs compared to traditional x86 tiers, provided software stacks are fully compiled and optimized for arm64. Workloads that fit memory constraints without saturating processor bounds can achieve strong resource efficiency.

This server instance is suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational and NoSQL databases, memory-resident analytics, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency backend services that benefit from large RAM pools without demanding specialized GPU compute.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-32 is a memory-focused virtual machine instance built on a 64-bit Arm processor architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy operations. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or attached graphics processing units, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage for persistent block data. Networking configurations do not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying arm64 hardware foundation offers resource and operational efficiency for applications compiled for Arm, delivering a large memory footprint without the overhead of oversized compute allocations. Workloads best aligned with the c4a-highmem-32 include in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-bound data processing frameworks, and high-concurrency microservices requiring sustained RAM access.
